explanation: Showing the soles of your feet or pointing them at someone is considered impolite mainly within Singapore's Malay and Indian communities, where feet are viewed as the lowest, least clean part of the body. It is not a universal taboo across all Singaporeans, especially in casual or Chinese-majority secular settings, but it's safest to keep your feet down and avoid pointing them at people or religious items.
local_tip: When sitting on the floor or low seating in a Malay or Indian home, tuck your feet under you or sit cross-legged rather than stretching your legs out toward others.
regional_note: The taboo is strongest in Malay-Muslim and Indian-Hindu households (feet seen as unclean, never pointed at people, prayer mats, or images); it is much less observed among Chinese or Westernized Singaporeans in everyday settings.

also_check.note: The feet are the lowest part of the body; pointing them at a person or a Buddha image is a serious taboo.
Showing the soles of your feet, even on furniture, is seen as casual rather than offensive.
Showing the soles of your feet to someone, such as while sitting cross-legged, is considered a clear insult.
